title: All Around Us, Fair with Flowers
description: All Around Us, Fair with Flowers in Tonic Solfa to STUTTGART, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 306, “Life's Work”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Eights and Sevens (8.7.8.7) (8.7.8.7), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to STUTTGART; any other Eights and Sevens (8.7.8.7) tune fits them as well.
underlay: All a-round us, fair with flo-wers, Fields of beau-ty sleep-ing lie; All a-round us clar-ion voi-ces Call to du-ty stern and high.

lines: All around us, fair with flowers,
Fields of beauty sleeping lie;
All around us clarion voices
Call to duty stern and high.
Thankfully we will rejoice in
All the beauty God has given;
But beware it does not win us
From the work ordained of Heaven.
Following every voice of mercy
With a trusting, loving heart;
Let us in life's earnest labor
Still be sure to do our part.
Now, to-day, and not to-morrow,
Let us work with all our might,
Lest the wretched faint and perish
In the coming stormy night.
Now, to-day, and not to-morrow, —
Lest, before to-morrow's sun,
We too, mournfully departing,
Shall have left our work undone.

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1848.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to STUTTGART by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
